subject: Wardrobes for sloped ceilings and alcoves
hook: No two loft ceilings share an angle. Here is how we capture yours.
ig:
No two loft ceilings share an angle. Here is how we capture yours.

A wardrobe under a slope only looks built in if the panels follow the ceiling. This is how we work:

On site: heights are taken along the slope, plus the knee wall, the depth and any windows or radiators.
On paper: the angle and heights go into your design, with long hanging under the tallest part and drawers where it drops.
In the workshop: side panels are cut to that angle on our panel saw, edged and assembled in Hanley.
On fitting day: our own team installs it and scribes the fillers to your ceiling and walls.

The last step matters more than people expect. Loft ceilings are rarely perfectly flat, and a scribed filler is what closes the line.

If a loft room is on your list for next year, now is a good time to start thinking. Comment LOFT and we will send you our wardrobes page.
fb:
A quick look at how we handle wardrobes in loft rooms, where nothing is square.

We take heights along the slope on site, draw the angle into your design, cut the side panels to match in our Hanley workshop, and scribe the final fillers to your ceiling on fitting day.

That is what makes the difference between a wardrobe pushed under a slope and one that looks like it was always there.
